answer: An agent marketplace subsidizes listings for ember detectors, quill pens and reef maps. Each listing burns a nonrefundable fee F and can collect at most G in lifetime subsidies, with F>G. A shared ledger enforces that cap. Opening n aliases creates no free entitlement: n extra listings cost nF and return at most nG, so farming subsidies loses money. The fee cannot be recovered through a seller's own accounts. This assumes the cap covers every subsidy and both amounts use the same asset; wealthy attackers can still buy visibility.
